title: XAT
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public XAT syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A city council argues that a new tram line will cut congestion because cities that have trams carry less traffic than cities that do not. Critics reply that wealthier cities are both more likely to build trams and better able to manage congestion by other means. The critics' response does which of the following?
options: Identifies an alternative cause that could explain the correlation the council relies on
Proves that trams have no effect on traffic in any city
Shows that the tram line will exceed its approved budget
Estimates the number of cars that the tram will remove
items.explanation: The council infers cause from a correlation across cities. The critics weaken that inference by pointing to wealth, which could independently produce both trams and lower congestion, so the correlation by itself cannot establish cause.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Four sentences form a coherent paragraph. Which sentence should come first? Sentence I - The report nevertheless insists that automation has raised overall employment in the sector. Sentence II - Several mills in the region closed last year after installing robotic looms. Sentence III - This claim rests on a survey of firms published in 2023. Sentence IV - The survey covered only those firms that had expanded their workforce.
options: Sentence I
Sentence II
Sentence III
Sentence IV
items.explanation: Sentence II states the job losses that the rest of the paragraph answers, and the word nevertheless in Sentence I can only refer back to those losses, so Sentence II must open the paragraph before the contrast makes sense.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: The board found the chief executive's reply so equivocal that its members could not decide whether she supported or opposed the merger. In this sentence, the word equivocal most nearly means
options: Passionate and firmly stated
Hostile and confrontational in tone
Open to more than one interpretation and deliberately unclear
Backed by detailed financial evidence
items.explanation: Equivocal describes language that can be read in opposing ways, which is exactly why the board could not determine her position, whereas the other choices all suggest a clarity or hostility that she did not show.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Which one of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
options: Neither of the two proposals have been accepted by the committee.
Neither of the two proposal has been accepted by the committee.
Neither of the two proposals has been accepting by the committee.
Neither of the two proposals has been accepted by the committee.
items.explanation: Neither is singular, so the verb must be has, and the perfect passive form has been accepted is required. The plural verb, the singular noun proposal and the active form accepting are all errors.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: During the merger call, the analyst let the cat out of the bag by mentioning the unpublished offer price. The phrase as used here means that he
options: Revealed a secret that was meant to stay hidden
Abandoned a project without giving warning
Admitted a mistake that he had made earlier
Created confusion among the listeners
items.explanation: To let the cat out of the bag is to disclose something confidential, which matches the analyst's mention of an unpublished price, while the other choices describe different kinds of disclosure or failure.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Since the library extended its weekend hours, weekend memberships have doubled. The library board therefore plans to extend weekday hours as well, expecting weekday memberships to double too. The plan depends on which of the following assumptions?
options: Weekend memberships were unusually low before the extension
Potential members value longer opening hours on weekdays as much as they do on weekends
The library's electricity costs will fall as opening hours increase
Doubled weekend memberships have already doubled the library's fee income
items.explanation: The board generalises a weekend result to weekdays, so it must assume that the two respond alike to longer hours. The other options are either irrelevant to the inference or would be conclusions rather than assumptions.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: An advertising agency claims that its new campaign caused higher sales because sales rose in every region where the campaign ran. Which consideration most undermines that claim?
options: The campaign ran for six months instead of three
The agency has won several awards for its earlier campaigns
Sales in those regions had already been rising for the four quarters before the campaign began
The campaign appeared on television as well as online
items.explanation: A pre-existing upward trend supplies a rival explanation for the rise, so the post campaign figures cannot isolate the effect of the campaign. Duration, past awards and media mix do not challenge the causal claim.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: An odometer is to distance travelled as a barometer is to
options: Air temperature
Vehicle speed
Relative humidity
Atmospheric pressure
items.explanation: An odometer records the distance a vehicle has covered and a barometer records atmospheric pressure, so the pair matches each instrument with the quantity it measures, while the other three quantities are measured by different instruments.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Find the next term in the letter series, A, C, F, J, O, which term comes next?
options: U
T
V
W
items.explanation: The gaps between letter positions grow by one each step, namely 2, 3, 4 and 5, so the next gap is 6 letters, and O advanced by six letters gives U.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: In a certain code, each letter of a word is replaced by the letter immediately following it in the alphabet, so PEN becomes QFO. How would HOUSE be written in that code?
options: GPVTF
IPTVF
IPVUE
JQWUG
items.explanation: Shifting every letter of HOUSE one place forward gives I, P, V, T and F, so the code is IPTVF. Shifting backwards or shifting only some of the letters produces the other three choices.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Consider the statements, all singers are artists, and some artists are painters. Which conclusion follows logically from these statements alone?
options: Some singers are painters
No artist is a singer
No conclusion about whether any singer is a painter can be drawn
All painters are artists
items.explanation: The premises link every singer to artists and only some artists to painters, leaving the link between singers and painters undetermined, so nothing specific follows; the other three claims go beyond the premises or contradict them.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Five officials P, Q, R, S and T address a panel exactly once each. P speaks before Q, P speaks before T, R speaks immediately after T, and S speaks last. Who speaks first?
options: T
Q
R
P
items.explanation: S is fixed in the last place and T must be immediately followed by R, while P has to come before both Q and T. That forces the opening speaker to be P, whichever valid order of the remaining officials is chosen.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: City X replaced free bus passes for students with a 50 percent discounted pass and reports that student bus ridership did not fall, concluding that the new scheme preserved ridership. Which statement, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: The number of students in the city grew by 15 percent while the number of student bus trips stayed the same
Neighbouring cities introduced a similar discount in the same year
The transport authority spent less on the discounted pass than on the free pass
Bus driver salaries were unchanged throughout the year
items.explanation: If the student population grew while trips stayed flat, trips per student actually fell, so ridership declined relative to need and the conclusion fails. The remaining statements do not bear on the ridership measure being claimed.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: The minister's explanation of the delay was so prolix that reporters stopped taking notes halfway through it. In this context, the word prolix means
options: Deliberately vague and evasive
Tediously lengthy and repetitious
Brief and to the point
Aggressive and accusatory
items.explanation: Prolix describes speech or writing that is unnecessarily long and dull, which explains why reporters gave up taking notes, and none of the other choices conveys the idea of excessive length.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Choose the sentence that most logically completes the paragraph. Remote work has expanded the talent pool available to many firms. Blank sentence. Yet managers still report that coordinating distributed teams takes deliberate effort. Which sentence fills the blank?
options: Teams therefore struggle to agree on meeting times across time zones
Most firms have consequently given up their central offices for good
Recruiters can now consider qualified applicants who could never have relocated for the role
Productivity monitoring software has become unnecessary in most teams
items.explanation: The word yet signals a contrast, so the blank must state a benefit of the wider talent pool. Teams struggling repeats the difficulty the final sentence raises instead of contrasting with it, the office claim is an unsupported absolute, and nothing in the paragraph shows monitoring became unnecessary.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Every firm that filed its return after 15 March was fined. No firm that paid within the statutory window was fined. Meridian filed its return on 20 March. Which conclusion must be true?
options: Meridian paid within the statutory window
Meridian's statutory auditors have been replaced
No firm that filed before 15 March was fined
Meridian was fined
items.explanation: Meridian filed after 15 March, and the first statement says that every such firm was fined, so Meridian must have been fined, which also rules out payment within the window. The third claim is unsupported and the fourth goes beyond the premises.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Which one of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
options: Having finished the audit, the team submitted its report to the board.
Having finished the audit, the report was submitted to the board.
Having finished the audit, it was the report that the team filed.
Having finished the audit, to file the report was the team's next action.
items.explanation: A participial phrase must describe the doer of the action, so only the first sentence attaches correctly. The others dangle the phrase from the report, from the pronoun it, or from an infinitive clause that never acts.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: A manufacturer withdrew a new snack from the market after its sales fell in the first month, concluding that consumers disliked the flavour. The reasoning above is flawed chiefly because it
options: Relies on opinions collected from the manufacturer's own employees
Treats a single month of sales as a reliable guide to consumer preference
Compares first month sales with full year sales of other products
Suggests that the snack should have been priced lower
items.explanation: Sales in a single month can be distorted by launch timing, distribution reach and promotion, so they cannot settle the question of taste. The remaining options describe flaws that this particular argument does not commit.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: Which one of the following words is the odd one out when compared with the other three?
options: Laconic
Terse
Garrulous
Pithy
items.explanation: Garrulous means excessively talkative, while laconic, terse and pithy all describe speech that is deliberately concise, so the first word does not belong with the other three.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: A restaurant replaced its printed menu with a QR code menu and reports that the average value of each table's order rose by 12 percent. Which statement, if true, most strongly supports the inference that the new menu caused the rise?
options: The restaurant raised the prices of all main courses by 8 percent that week
The cost of printing menus increased during the same period
The QR code menu lists exactly the same dishes as the printed menu
Tables using the QR code menu ordered more side dishes and desserts than tables that requested a printed menu
items.explanation: Evidence that QR users actually added more items supplies a direct mechanism for the higher order values. The price rise offers a rival explanation, printing costs are irrelevant to the claim, and identical listings are neutral.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Verbal and Logical Ability

items.stem: A regional head learns that a high performing sales manager repeatedly humiliates junior colleagues in review meetings, and three members of his team have asked for transfers. The quarter's targets have still been met. What should the regional head do first?
options: Meet the manager with specific documented instances, set clear behavioural expectations and review progress within a month
Promote the manager to a national role so that he no longer works with the same juniors
Take no action because the team continues to meet its sales targets
Transfer the three juniors to other regions without discussing the manager's conduct
items.explanation: Hitting targets does not excuse humiliation, and ignoring it signals approval while transferring the complainants punishes those who spoke up. The manager must be confronted with evidence and held to a defined standard with a review date.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A component supplier's last three deliveries showed defect rates of 4, 5 and 6 percent, still inside the 7 percent contractual limit. Rework costs 40 rupees per unit, while qualifying an alternative supplier takes six months. The purchase manager should
options: Accept the deliveries as compliant because the contractual limit has not been breached
Issue a corrective action notice with a defect reduction target and a requalification trigger, while screening and reworking current stock
Switch to a new supplier immediately and place the first order this week
Raise the contractual defect limit to 8 percent to give the supplier more headroom
items.explanation: The upward trend inside the permitted limit still threatens the production line, so the response must contain current stock while correcting the supplier and keeping a fallback ready. Passively accepting or loosening the contract removes all leverage.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A health drink company wants an advertisement in which a doctor says that users of the drink feel more energetic. The statement is literally true and backed by customer feedback, but no clinical trial supports any health benefit. The marketing head should
options: Run the advertisement because every individual statement in it is literally true
Add the doctor's name and qualifications to make the claim more persuasive
Replace the health claim with factual product information that the available evidence actually supports
Shift the advertisement to print media where advertising rules are applied less strictly
items.explanation: Literal truth does not rescue an advertisement that leaves an unsupported health impression, so the claim must be removed or confined to what the evidence shows. Greater prominence and a different medium do not fix the underlying defect.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: While auditing a listed company, you find a tax arrangement that is lawful but would surprise the company's lenders if they knew of it. The finance director asks you to leave it out of the audit report. As engagement partner you should
options: Leave it out of the report because the arrangement is lawful
Tell the finance director that the omission is acceptable if he signs a note
Resign immediately without giving any reason to the board
Evaluate the arrangement's effect on the financial statements and report the matter to the audit committee
items.explanation: Lawfulness does not settle disclosure, and the effect on lender covenants may be material, so the issue must be assessed and escalated to those charged with governance. Silent omission breaches professional duty and an unexplained resignation helps nobody.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: The head of procurement discovers that the lowest bid for a critical component, 12 percent below the next bid, comes from a firm owned by his cousin. He has not influenced the specification. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Disclose the relationship in writing and recuse himself so that an independent panel evaluates the bid
Approve the bid because it is the lowest and the specification was not influenced
Reject the cousin's bid outright and award the contract to the next bidder
Ask his cousin to withdraw the bid so that the conflict does not arise
items.explanation: Disclosure with recusal preserves both the saving and the integrity of the process. Silent approval leaves an apparent bias, outright rejection discards a legitimate offer without evaluation, and hiding the bid still conceals the conflict.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A supermarket faces long weekend queues because all staff work the same fixed shift, while the weekday counters are half empty. The store manager has no extra headcount budget. The best response is to
options: Hire additional permanent staff to cover the weekend rush
Stagger shifts to match weekend peaks and cross train staff so that any counter can be opened
Limit the number of customers allowed inside the store at weekends
Do nothing because weekday understaffing balances weekend overcrowding
items.explanation: Rephasing the same workforce against demand and widening skills adds capacity at peak times at no extra cost. Extra hires exceed the budget, entry limits turn customers away, and doing nothing leaves the complaint unresolved.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A loyal employee with fifteen years of service no longer uses the current software stack, and his module now has the highest defect rate in the department. What should his manager do?
options: Start termination proceedings immediately because his output has declined
Move him to a ceremonial role with no delivery responsibilities to reward his loyalty
Put him on a time bound upskilling plan with clear milestones while reallocating his critical tasks during the transition
Wait for the annual appraisal and record the problem in his review
items.explanation: Service loyalty and a real performance gap together call for a managed fix that protects delivery while restoring competence. Dismissal wastes experience, a ceremonial role hides the issue, and deferring to appraisal lets defects reach customers.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: After a flood cuts road access, a grocery store finds that the wholesale price of essentials has risen by only 10 percent, but the owner is considering tripling shelf prices because demand far exceeds supply. The most appropriate course is to
options: Triple prices because the market will bear them and the law does not forbid it
Stop selling essentials altogether until road access is restored
Buy stock from distant districts at inflated prices so that shelves stay full at normal rates
Keep pre flood prices, limit quantities per household and seek reimbursement for any genuine cost increase
items.explanation: Holding prices with rationing prevents profiteering from a disaster while covering real cost increases. Tripling exploits stranded customers, withdrawing supply worsens the shortage, and paying inflated freight destroys the margin the store needs.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: An analysis shows that customers who use discount coupons spend less per order and are less profitable. The chief executive proposes banning coupons for everyone from next month. Which approach is best?
options: Segment coupon users by acquisition cost and run controlled tests before deciding on any blanket ban
Ban coupons for all customers from the first of next month
Double the coupon value for everyone to lift volumes quickly
Continue the current coupon programme unchanged because it drives traffic
items.explanation: The aggregate figure may hide profitable segments, so segmentation and testing separate correlation from causation before a hard to reverse decision. A blanket ban and a blanket increase both act on an unexamined average, and status quo ignores the signal.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A factory expansion will create 200 local jobs but will add lorries to a narrow village road. The village council has threatened to protest, while the state industry ministry wants quick approval. What should the company do?
options: Abandon the expansion in view of the village council's objections
Publish the traffic impact study, commit to mitigation such as a separate access road and staggered shifts, and seek conditional approval
Begin construction before any impact study so that the jobs are not delayed
Promise the jobs to a different district and close the village negotiation
items.explanation: Conditional approval with a published assessment and concrete mitigation balances jobs against safety and keeps both stakeholders engaged. Abandonment wastes the investment, skipping the study invites legal challenge, and moving the site abandons the community that raised concerns.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A festive season sale is six weeks away and the supplier's lead time is also six weeks. The demand forecast ranges from 8000 to 14000 units, and unsold stock would block working capital for months. What ordering strategy is best?
options: Order 14000 units now so that no possible sale is lost
Place no order and buy from the spot market once the forecast is exact
Place a base order for the lower forecast and secure a contractual option to increase quantities at a fixed price before a cut off date
Repeat last year's order quantity without revisiting the forecast
items.explanation: A base commitment plus a priced option covers the downside while preserving upside flexibility, which suits the uncertainty. Full stocking risks dead stock, spot buying risks unavailability, and repeating history ignores changed demand.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: An e-commerce subscription team finds that new customers subscribe in two taps but cancellation requires a phone call during working hours. Churn is falling and the team proposes keeping the process as it is. What should the product head do?
options: Keep the phone only process because competitors use similar tactics
Move the cancellation link deeper into the settings menu to reduce churn further
Charge a cancellation fee that was not disclosed at the time of sign up
Make cancellation available in the app in the same number of steps as sign up
items.explanation: Consumer protection norms and customer trust both require an exit as easy as entry, and deliberately obstructive design invites regulatory penalty and long term brand damage. Adding friction or imposing hidden fees compounds the same defect.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A board asks for a 10 percent headcount cut. One delivery unit is overstaffed after a client left, another runs at full capacity on a critical product, and hiring has already been frozen. What sequence of actions is most defensible?
options: Move surplus staff from the idle unit into the critical product after short retraining, then consider voluntary separation before any forced cuts
Cut 10 percent of staff in every unit so that the burden is shared equally
Retrench the whole idle unit at once to finish the exercise quickly
Outsource the critical product team so that its headcount disappears from the books
items.explanation: Redeployment keeps scarce skills in the business and meets the target before involuntary exits. Equal percentage cuts damage the productive unit, blanket retrenchment discards recoverable capacity, and outsourcing a critical product merely transfers risk.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: Before a contract renewal, a supplier's regional manager offers the procurement manager a personal festival bonus of one month's salary and makes clear that the renewal is expected. What should the procurement manager do?
options: Accept the bonus because the supplier's prices are competitive anyway
Decline the personal payment and ask that any commercial concession be documented as a rebate to the company
Accept the bonus but report it only after the contract has been renewed
Reject the bonus and cancel the renewal without evaluating other suppliers
items.explanation: A personal benefit tied to a decision creates an undeclared conflict and criminal exposure, so it must be refused with any value redirected to the firm. Delayed disclosure is still concealment, and cancelling a good contract punishes the business rather than the briber.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A loyal customer's refrigerator fails ten days outside the warranty period. Replacement parts are unavailable and the model has been discontinued. The service head should
options: Refuse the claim because the unit is outside the warranty period
Offer double the purchase price in cash as compensation
Authorise a goodwill replacement with a comparable model within a defined service recovery limit and record the reason
Ask the customer to post a public review describing the failure before any decision
items.explanation: A bounded goodwill gesture recovers the relationship at controlled cost. A flat refusal risks a valuable customer and possible escalation, an exaggerated payout is disproportionate, and linking help to publicity turns service into a transaction.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A growth team wants to promote a new plan by text message to 500000 numbers bought from a data vendor, promising high conversion. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Send the messages after 9 pm so that fewer recipients complain
Send from a new sender identity and stop as soon as complaints begin
Rely on the vendor's claim that the list is pre consented and send to all numbers
Send only to customers who have given prior consent for such messages and suppress every number on the Do Not Disturb registry
items.explanation: Consent and registered preferences are the only defensible basis for bulk messaging. Timing and sender changes do not cure the absence of consent, while a vendor's unverified claim merely shifts the liability onto the sending firm.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A batch of structural material fails a lab strength test by a narrow margin. The project deadline is tight and the client is pressing for release of the batch for non critical work. The project manager should
options: Quarantine the batch and have it retested by an accredited laboratory before any release, accepting the possible delay
Release the batch because the shortfall is marginal and the work is non critical
Ask the original laboratory to revise its certificate to show a pass
Blend the failed batch with conforming material so that average results pass
items.explanation: Independent verification protects safety and the firm's position. Releasing unverified material risks failure, asking a laboratory to revise a result is falsification, and blending hides non conformance rather than resolving it.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: An executive finds that her team has been billing a client for hours that were never worked, and the practice is condoned by her manager, who is a close friend. What should she do?
options: Raise it informally with her manager only and take no further step
Report the matter through the designated audit or grievance channel with the timesheet evidence attached
Inform the client directly before telling anyone internally
Wait until after her appraisal to avoid spoiling her relationship with the team
items.explanation: Documented reporting through the proper channel protects both the firm and the client and gives the allegation a fair process. Private discussion risks concealment, going straight to the client breaches internal duty, and delay lets the practice continue.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A chain store's branch inside a mall is loss making. The landlord offers a 30 percent rent reduction only if the chain signs a five year lease with no exit clause. What is the best response?
options: Refuse to negotiate because the branch is loss making anyway
Sign the five year lease in order to obtain immediate cost relief
Counter with a shorter lease that ties rent to a share of sales and includes a break option after two years
Close the branch immediately and forfeit the deposit
items.explanation: A revenue linked, time limited deal reduces fixed cost while preserving flexibility, which addresses the loss without creating a larger long term liability. Refusal, an unbreakable lock in and an immediate exit all trade one problem for another.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A startup has six months of runway left and three proposals on the table, an enterprise pilot with a large client, an across the board discount campaign and an acquisition approach. What is the most appropriate course?
options: Cut prices by 30 percent across the board to lift revenue immediately
Open acquisition talks at once so that the company is sold before exploring revenue
Spend the remaining runway on brand advertising to build awareness
Run the enterprise pilot as a paid proof of concept with a six week cap and a clear go or no go decision point
items.explanation: A paid pilot converts scarce time into evidence and possibly revenue with a built in decision gate. Blanket discounts buy low value revenue, selling early abandons upside, and advertising spends cash with no measurable return inside the runway.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Decision Making

items.stem: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40 percent above cost price and then allows a discount of 20 percent on the marked price. His profit percentage is
options: 12 percent
20 percent
10 percent
18 percent
items.explanation: The selling price is 1.40 times 0.80 times cost, that is 1.12 times cost, so the profit is 12 percent. Ignoring either the markup or the discount step produces the other three choices.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: Two vessels contain mixtures of milk and water in the ratios 3 to 1 and 5 to 2 respectively. Equal quantities of the two mixtures are combined. The ratio of milk to water in the resulting mixture is
options: 8 to 3
17 to 7
items.explanation: The milk fractions are three fourths and five sevenths, whose average for equal volumes is 41/56, leaving 15/56 water, so the ratio is 41 to 15. Averaging the two ratios directly gives the distractors.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: The cost price of 12 articles is equal to the selling price of 15 articles. The seller incurs a loss of
options: 25 percent
16.67 percent
20 percent
12.5 percent
items.explanation: The selling price of one article is twelve fifteenths of its cost, that is 0.8 times cost, so the loss is 20 percent. Taking fifteen twelfths as the ratio instead would wrongly show a gain.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: A train 180 metres long crosses a platform 320 metres long in 40 seconds. The speed of the train is
options: 54 km per hour
40 km per hour
36 km per hour
45 km per hour
items.explanation: The train covers its own length plus the platform, that is 500 metres, in 40 seconds, giving 12.5 metres per second which equals 45 km per hour. Timing only the train length or only the platform length gives the other values.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: A can finish a piece of work in 12 days and B can finish the same work in 18 days. They work together for 4 days after which A leaves. The time B takes to finish the remaining work is
options: 8 days
6 days
9 days
10 days
items.explanation: Together they finish 5/36 of the work per day, so in 4 days they complete 5/9 and 4/9 remains. B alone does 1/18 per day, so he needs 4/9 times 18, that is 8 days.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum of 10000 rupees at 10 percent per annum for 2 years is
options: 110 rupees
100 rupees
50 rupees
200 rupees
items.explanation: Simple interest yields 12000 rupees and compound interest yields 12100 rupees over two years, so the difference is 100 rupees, which is also the second year's interest on the first year's interest of 1000 rupees.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: The average of 11 numbers is 50. The average of the first six of them is 47 and the average of the last six is 55. The sixth number is
items.explanation: The total of all 11 numbers is 550, the first six total 282 and the last six total 330. The sixth number is counted in both groups, so it equals 282 plus 330 minus 550, that is 62.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: A right angled triangle has legs of length 9 cm and 12 cm. The radius of the circle inscribed in the triangle is
options: 4 cm
2.5 cm
6 cm
3 cm
items.explanation: The hypotenuse is 15 cm, and the inradius of a right triangle is the sum of the legs minus the hypotenuse, divided by two, that is (9 plus 12 minus 15) divided by 2, which is 3 cm.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: A solid cylinder has a height equal to its base diameter. If its volume is 432 pi cubic cm, its base radius is
options: 6 cm
12 cm
3 cm
8 cm
items.explanation: With height equal to twice the radius, the volume is 2 pi r cubed, so 2 r cubed = 432 and r cubed = 216, giving a radius of 6 cm; forgetting the factor of two leads to a different cube root.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: The remainder when 7 raised to the power 100 is divided by 5 is
items.explanation: 7 is congruent to 2 modulo 5, and the powers of 2 repeat every four steps, so an exponent of 100, being a multiple of 4, gives a remainder of 1; the other remainders come from ignoring the cycle.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one of the numbers is 60, the other number is
items.explanation: The product of two numbers equals their HCF times their LCM, so the other number is 12 times 360 divided by 60, which is 72; the distractors arise from dividing or multiplying the wrong pair of quantities.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: If x + 1/x = 5, then the value of x^2 + 1/x^2 is
items.explanation: Squaring both sides of x + 1/x = 5 gives x^2 + 2 + 1/x^2 = 25, so x^2 + 1/x^2 = 23; forgetting to subtract the middle term of 2 gives the distractor 25.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: The roots of the equation x^2 - 5x + c = 0 differ by 1. The value of c is
items.explanation: Two roots that differ by 1 and add up to 5 must be 3 and 2, so their product c is 6; using the sum alone or the difference alone gives the other choices.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: The number of distinct arrangements of the letters of the word LEVEL is
items.explanation: LEVEL has five letters in which L and E each appear twice, so the arrangements are 5 factorial divided by 2 factorial twice, that is 120 divided by 4, giving 30; ignoring the repeated letters gives 120.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: Two fair dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers on them is 9 is
items.explanation: The favourable outcomes are 3 plus 6, 4 plus 5, 5 plus 4 and 6 plus 3, that is four of the thirty six equally likely outcomes, which reduces to 1/9; the other fractions come from miscounting the pairs.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: In a class of 60 students, 35 play cricket, 28 play football and 10 play neither. The number who play both games is
items.explanation: Students who play at least one game number 50, while 35 plus 28 is 63, so the overlap is 63 minus 50, that is 13; forgetting to remove the group that plays neither gives 23.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: A firm reported quarterly revenue and operating cost in lakh rupees as follows. Quarter 1 revenue 120 cost 96, Quarter 2 revenue 150 cost 120, Quarter 3 revenue 140 cost 119, Quarter 4 revenue 180 cost 135. The operating margin in Quarter 3 is
options: 15 percent
12.5 percent
18 percent
20 percent
items.explanation: Quarter 3 profit is 140 minus 119, that is 21, and 21 divided by revenue of 140 gives 15 percent; using cost as the base or borrowing another quarter's margin gives the distractors.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: A product's annual unit sales rose from 8000 in 2021 to 10648 in 2024. The compound annual growth rate over these three years is
options: 8 percent
10 percent
12 percent
11 percent
items.explanation: 8000 times 1.10 cubed equals 10648, so growth at 10 percent each year compounds exactly to the observed figure, while 8, 11 and 12 percent give different three year totals.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: A retailer sells three grades of tea at 400, 500 and 600 rupees per kg in the ratio 2 to 3 to 5. The average selling price per kg is
options: 500 rupees
550 rupees
530 rupees
525 rupees
items.explanation: The weighted total is 2 times 400 plus 3 times 500 plus 5 times 600, that is 5300 over 10 kg, giving 530 rupees per kg; the unweighted average of the three prices is 500.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation

items.stem: A website recorded unique visits from Monday to Friday as 1200, 1500, 1350, 1440 and 1800 respectively. The percentage increase in visits from Thursday to Friday is
options: 20 percent
30 percent
15 percent
25 percent
items.explanation: Visits rose from 1440 to 1800, an increase of 360, and 360 divided by the Thursday base of 1440 gives 25 percent; dividing by the Friday figure instead gives the distractor of 20 percent.
items.reference: XAT Syllabus - Quantitative Ability and Data Interpretation
